declared_purpose: Provide managed game mining through OpenClaw tool HTTP APIs using a user-supplied in-game apiCode, with credential caching, mining and stamina operations, session events, status and safe stopping. Authentication, credential-management tools and session reporting are explicit features; automatic caching during other calls, raw response retention and process-global access are implementation choices. Sources: SKILL.md:18-45,70-168.

data_operations.data_scope: apiCode, cacheKey, language, loop settings, event cursor and optional session identifiers
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: index.js request handler and process memory
data_operations.condition: POST /tool/:name; invalid schema returns 400. The packaged start command runs this handler.

data_operations.source: set_api_code input and existing credential store
data_operations.data_scope: cacheKey-to-apiCode mappings, serialized without application-level encryption
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: apiCodeCache and API_CODE_STORE_PATH, default ./data/api-code-store.json; writes first use a temporary file beside the store
data_operations.condition: set_api_code writes the complete cache; startup loads all stored entries. Explicit credential persistence is a documented feature.

data_operations.operation: Automatically cache credentials supplied to other tools
data_operations.source: Explicit apiCode in operational tool requests
data_operations.data_scope: apiCode under the supplied or default cacheKey
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: apiCodeCache and the complete on-disk credential store
data_operations.condition: check_mining_state, buy_stamina, get_stamina or either managed-loop start receives apiCode; persistence precedes the upstream action and the already-running-loop check.

data_operations.operation: Read and return a cached credential
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: get_api_code caller through its HTTP response
data_operations.condition: The requested key exists. This is an explicitly documented credential-read tool; the response alone does not establish onward disclosure.

data_operations.recipient_or_storage: In-memory cache and rewritten credential store
data_operations.condition: clear_api_code deletes an existing entry. An active task separately holds apiCode; clearing the cache does not erase that captured value or invoke upstream revocation.

data_operations.operation: Authenticate direct game operations and return their responses
data_operations.source: Explicit apiCode or cached fallback; upstream game responses
data_operations.data_scope: apiCode in X-Api-Code; empty JSON request bodies; complete returned JSON for mining state, stamina purchase or stamina and diamonds
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Game API at GAME_API_BASE_URL, default https://api.km.cocweb3.com; returned JSON goes to the requesting tool caller
data_operations.condition: check_mining_state, buy_stamina or get_stamina resolves a credential. Authentication and these operations are explicit requirements.

data_operations.source: Resolved apiCode, loop options and game responses
data_operations.data_scope: apiCode header; enabled boolean for setAutoMining; empty bodies for startMining and endMining; returned timing and reward data
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured game API; loop-local memory and callbacks
data_operations.condition: Either start tool starts a loop. setAutoMining(true) is attempted before execution and false during finalization; rounds start, wait and claim rewards. Retry timing and stop limits govern repeated calls. The loop uses endMining results as checkState rather than making a separate checkMiningState request each round.

data_operations.operation: Check resources and optionally purchase stamina automatically
data_operations.source: Upstream insufficient-stamina error and subsequent resource responses
data_operations.data_scope: apiCode header; stamina, diamonds and maxStamina snapshot; purchase result
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured game API /api/getStamina and conditionally /api/buyStamina; transient loop memory
data_operations.condition: Auto-buy is enabled and the loop catches GameApiHttpError with code 2003. Full stamina avoids purchase; nonpositive diamonds prevents purchase. Failure counts limit retries. postJson creates this error for non-2xx HTTP responses, so a code-2003 body with HTTP success alone does not trigger this branch.

data_operations.operation: Read public display configuration and derive reward labels
data_operations.source: ORE_TYPE_NAME_MAP_PATH, default ./config/ore-type-map.json; reward oreType and selected language
data_operations.data_scope: Public ore identifiers and translations; locally derived oreTypeName
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: tools.js map cache and enriched reward response
data_operations.condition: endMining response enrichment loads the map once; missing or unsupported language uses zh_CN. Language selection is explicit/default configuration, not an inferred personal attribute.

data_operations.operation: Associate session identifiers and retain operational history
data_operations.source: Session header or body, cacheKey, loop callbacks and endMining response
data_operations.data_scope: Session key, timestamps, round/error counts, reward objects, full lastCheckState and unprojected commonInfo or playerStatus
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Process-global managedMiningStatus and bounded in-memory event array
data_operations.condition: Both start tools extract the session key, preferring x-openclaw-session-key, then openclawSessionKey, then sessionKey. Round completion retains upstream state and appends rewards/player status. Old events are shifted past the configured limit, default 200; completion retains final status until replacement or process termination.

data_operations.operation: Return status, events and derived summaries
data_operations.data_scope: Full status and retained upstream data; incremental events and session key; quick status subset; reward totals and displayed Gold balance
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Calling HTTP client; no additional recipient is established by the return
data_operations.condition: Start, stop, already-running errors and full-status tools return status; event reads filter only by sinceEventId. Quick status omits raw rewards/player state. These handlers do not match the requesting session against the stored session key.

data_operations.source: Upstream error responses and execution exceptions
data_operations.data_scope: HTTP status, upstream response body or error message; non-2xx response bodies embedded in GameApiHttpError.message
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Tool caller; managed status/events for loop errors; process console for setAutoMining failures
data_operations.condition: Direct errors return the upstream object or message. Loop errors can become lastError and event payloads. Failed automatic-mining toggles log the error object. Actual response contents and console retention are unspecified.

data_operations.source: Failed tool invocation and associated diagnostics
data_operations.data_scope: HTTP status, response body, tool name, cacheKey, timestamps and logs
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Agent's failure report; report destination and persistence are unspecified
data_operations.condition: The entry document explicitly requests reporting tool failures or unexpected behavior. The supplied server source does not implement a separate report delivery channel.

potential_excess.data_scope: Explicit apiCode supplied for an individual query, purchase or loop start
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: API_CODE_STORE_PATH credential file and its temporary write file
potential_excess.condition: Operational calls receive apiCode, including a start request subsequently rejected because a loop is already running.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The operational request needs authentication. Persistence is explicitly offered by set_api_code; the other tools document explicit credentials or cached fallback without requiring every supplied credential to be saved.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Resolve a credential and authenticate the requested game operation; retain a loop credential in memory while the loop needs it.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Persist only through set_api_code or an explicit save choice. Avoid the separate disk-write action during ordinary authenticated calls.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep documented set/get/clear caching and cached fallback functional; preserve the running loop's credential lifetime.

potential_excess.data_scope: Complete endMining response, unprojected commonInfo/playerStatus and all fields of each reward object
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: managedMiningStatus.lastCheckState, lastPlayerStatus, reward arrays and event history; subsequently full-status/event callers
potential_excess.condition: A round completes; player status is repeated in round events and final state is retained after stopping.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Recording rewards and reporting managed-session status are explicit features. Retaining every upstream field is an implementation choice; actual additional fields are unknown.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Keep round outcomes, timing, errors and reward details needed for documented status, including Gold used in the friendly message.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Project upstream responses into a documented status schema and keep only needed reward/player fields. Avoid retaining a parallel full response and repeating unnecessary player fields in events.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Confirm upstream schemas and legitimate full-status consumers before removing fields. Preserve required reward display and event semantics; the supplied source cannot establish which unknown upstream fields are sensitive or required.

potential_excess.data_scope: Cached credentials and another session's identifiers, rewards, player state and diagnostics
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: A different caller able to reach the same service's credential, status, event or control endpoints
potential_excess.condition: The process serves multiple trust domains without an external access boundary. The code selects credentials by caller-supplied/default cacheKey and returns global session state without checking session ownership.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: OpenClaw session binding and credential access are documented; cross-session access is not required for managed mining.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Allow the authorized caller to manage its credential and retrieve its session status/events.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Scope cache and session lookups to an authenticated caller/session; enforce ownership before returning credentials or global status, including conflict and stop responses.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain authorized get_api_code and session reporting. This is a conditional recipient-scope excess; deployment isolation and external authentication are unknown, so actual cross-user disclosure is unproven.

potential_excess.data_scope: Complete non-2xx upstream response body embedded in an error message
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Loop lastError and error/stopped events, later returned through status/event tools
potential_excess.condition: A game request fails with non-2xx HTTP status and its message reaches loop error handling.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Failure reporting and retry control are needed, but storing the whole upstream body as a status string is not necessary for counting errors or identifying an error code.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Retain actionable error code, operation, HTTP status and a safe summary.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Construct structured, allowlisted error summaries for routine status/events; restrict raw diagnostic detail to an explicit diagnostic path with redaction.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep required failure reporting and troubleshooting useful. Unknown upstream body contents prevent asserting that credentials or personal fields are actually present.

potential_excess.data_scope: Error object containing upstream responseBody and potentially a body-bearing message
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Process console output for failed setApiAutoMining attempts
potential_excess.condition: The start or finalization toggle fails and console.warn receives the whole error object.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Recording toggle failure supports operation and troubleshooting; unrestricted upstream payload logging is an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Record which toggle failed, HTTP/server code and a safe diagnostic summary.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Log selected error fields and redact unrestricted response content rather than passing the complete error object.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve useful failure diagnostics. Console collection, retention and actual sensitive content remain unknown.

unknowns: Upstream response schemas, server-side processing, credential retention, purchase/mining persistence and deletion behavior are not supplied. These block field-level necessity and downstream-retention conclusions.
Runtime GAME_API_BASE_URL overrides, service exposure, caller identity, external authentication and deployment isolation are unknown. Actual cross-session access cannot be established.
Credential-file permissions, storage encryption outside the application, backups, failed-write temporary-file retention and physical erasure are unknown.
Console collection/retention and the destination or persistence of agent-generated failure reports are unspecified.

Dependency implementations and installation behavior are outside the supplied source. package.json and package-lock.json identify dependencies and registry artifacts but do not establish their data handling.
The supplied-source audit is complete. External behavior and deployment-dependent exposure remain unresolved; no redundant upstream mining or stamina request is established.
